title: SPEC-059 extension of the orchestration settings: push transports, kill switch and resolved delivery (draft, not adopted)
description: SPEC-059 does not redefine scopes, modes or strategies. SPEC-057's orchestration-settings schema owns conversation, repository and user scopes, notificationMode (pull or push), notificationStrategy (mailbox-whisper, megaphone or doorbell), guardMode, the precedence (the most specific scope wins; a block guard mode at repository or user scope is a floor) and operator ownership, and it carries a versioned extensions member keyed by owner specification. This schema defines what SPEC-059 stores under extensions.SPEC-059 (the top-level validation target: an extension entry with extensionVersion agent-braid-push-settings/v0.1 and a bounded settings object) and, in $defs.resolvedDelivery, the result that the SPEC-059 resolver produces from the SPEC-057 resolved record. Composition is two-step and is part of the planned tests: the whole settings record validates against the SPEC-057 schema (which stores the entry without interpreting it), and the entry validates against this schema. Megaphone (monitor-stdout or channel) and Doorbell (session-socket-self) are the only push strategies; both are opt-in. Push is effective only when every enabling condition holds; otherwise the effective mode is pull with each unmet condition named from the closed list. The default Mailbox + Whisper strategy needs no SPEC-059 push: the Mailbox is the pull notice and the Whisper is a SPEC-058 companion output.

transportId.description: The SPEC-059 push transports. monitor-stdout and channel are the Megaphone; session-socket-self is the Doorbell. The Whisper carrier (hook additional context) is the SPEC-058 companion's and is not a SPEC-059 push option.

pushSettings.description: Member names and value shapes satisfy the SPEC-057 extensionEntry bounds (scalars and short lists of short strings). pushTransports is an ordered preference; a transport without a passing receipt, or one that does not belong to the requested strategy, is skipped and never assumed. killSwitch true at any scope or at the top level disables every SPEC-059 push; like the block guard mode it is a floor that a more specific scope cannot lower (a planning interpretation of the founder's floor rule, to be confirmed in the G2 review).

resolvedDelivery.description: Result of the SPEC-059 resolver. It consumes the SPEC-057 resolved settings (consumedFromSPEC057) and completes the member that SPEC-057 records as reserved-for-SPEC-059. The mapping is: not-requested stays not-requested; reserved-for-SPEC-059 becomes active or unavailable. The resolver performs no network, socket or process operation and never reports an unavailable push as active.

effectiveDelivery.description: mailbox is the pull notice that the orchestrator reads; megaphone and doorbell appear only when push is active.

path.description: Repository-relative receipt location in a conservative ASCII set, so that no control, bidirectional, format or tag character can occur; the same anchor rejects a final line feed, which a plain dollar anchor would accept under Python.

recordedAfterG2Adoption.description: True when the passing probe receipt was pinned after the founder recorded adoption of the G2 contract. Required for the Doorbell.
